title: Evidence Index & Entitlement Forensics Playbook
author: Aisha Collins
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a company-wide evidence index and the entitlement snapshot model used to collect, classify, preserve, and hand off forensic artifacts during security incidents that may impact model serving, data residency, or customer isolation. It unifies requirements for RBAC, audit logging, SDLC hooks, retention, and exception handling so that evidence is admissible for audits and legal review while preserving privacy and residency constraints.

Goals:
- Provide a canonical evidence catalog (the "Forensic Bag") for incident responders and compliance teams.
- Define RBAC-based entitlement snapshots to capture who could access what at the time of an incident.
- Specify immutable logging and storage requirements across geographic regions.
- Ensure secure handoff of artifacts to legal, regulators, or customers with provable chain-of-custody.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents that require preservation of logs, entitlements, model snapshots, or ingress/egress traces across hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.
- Not intended for routine operational debugging; use the standard debug runbooks for non-forensic cases.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Security Incident Response (SIR) team (pager: #sir-oncall).
- Evidence curator: Compliance Engineering (responsible for packaging and redaction).
- Legal & Privacy: consulted for regulatory disclosures.
- Escalation path: SIR -> Head of Security -> General Counsel (15 min for high-severity incidents).

Forensic Bag: canonical artifact index
Each incident must produce a Forensic Bag manifest (JSON) that lists collected artifacts and their metadata. Minimum fields in manifest (examples shown):

Example manifest (trimmed):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2027-0423",
  "collected_at": "2027-02-11T14:23:00Z",
  "collector": "sir-agent-v2",
  "artifacts": [
    { "type": "audit-log-chunk", "path": "s3://forensics/inc-2027/chunk-1.ndjson.gpg", "sha256": "...", "region": "us-west-2" },
    { "type": "entitlement-snapshot", "path": "s3://forensics/inc-2027/ent-snap-20270211.json.gpg", "redacted": "true" }
  ]
}

Artifact types and retention mapping:
| Artifact type | Minimum retention | Storage class | Notes |
|---------------|-------------------:|---------------|-------|
| Immutable audit logs (ndjson) | 7 years | Immutable WORM bucket | Geo-tagged; include schema version |
| Entitlement snapshots | 3 years | Encrypted object store | Redact PII; store regionally |
| Model checkpoints (serving) | 1 year | Encrypted object store | Version + quant profile |
| Network captures (pcap) | 90 days | Restricted archive | Only when approved by Legal |
| CI build artifacts (signed) | 5 years | Immutable build store | Required for SDLC evidence |

RBAC & entitlement snapshot model:
- Snapshot goal: reconstruct effective access graph at incident timestamp (subject -> role(s) -> bindings -> resources).
- Snapshot components: user/service principal list, role definitions (with permission sets), binding timestamps, ephemeral activation records, delegated approvals.
- Snapshot generation methods:
  1) Live snapshot via entitlement service API: `GET /v1/entitlements/snapshot?ts=2027-02-11T14:00:00Z`
  2) Fallback: reconstruct from audit events + identity provider (IdP) tokens.

RBAC snapshot fields (JSON lines recommended):
- principal_id, principal_type, active_roles, bound_resources, activation_window, source (idp/ldap/service), evidence_refs

Audit logging requirements:
1) Schema and context: Every request to a model-serving endpoint must emit an audit event containing: timestamp, request_id, principal_id (or service_id), model_id and model_version, route, sequence_length, tokens_generated, response_hash, request_headers (redacted), region, tenant_id (if multi-tenant). Use schema v2.1.
2) Immutability: Audit logs MUST be written to an append-only store with WORM capability. Logs are signed and chunked every 100K events.
3) Tamper-evidence: Each chunk is sha256-signed and stored with key rotation metadata. Verify using KMS public key for chain-of-trust.
4) Access controls: Only SIR and Compliance Engineering have cross-region read for forensic bundles. Dev teams have read access scoped to their tenant and timeframe.

Data residency and redaction:
- Principle: Evidence storage region must follow data residency constraints of the affected tenant. If an incident involves cross-border data, the manifest must include a residency rationale and Legal approval id.
- Redaction policy: PII and customer-sensitive fields must be redacted in artifacts prior to export unless Legal directs otherwise. Use automated redaction pipeline with audit logs to show what was removed.
- Encryption: All forensic artifacts must be encrypted at rest and in-transit using customer-managed keys for private deployments or company KMS for hosted artifacts.

Secure SDLC hooks for evidence collection:
- CI build artifacts must embed provenance metadata (build id, git sha, signed artifact). Example YAML snippet to include in pipeline:
```
provenance:
  build_id: ${BUILD_ID}
  git_sha: ${GIT_COMMIT}
  signer: ci-signer@redwood-infra
```
- Deployment approvals: deployment records (who approved, when, permit id) are required evidence for incidents linked to configuration drift.

Incident response procedure (evidence-centric):
1) Triage & scope determination (SIR)
   - Assign incident_id and create Forensic Bag manifest stub.
   - Determine residency constraints and initial legal classification.
2) Entitlement snapshot
   - Generate RBAC snapshot for T-5min to T+5min around suspected event.
   - If live API unavailable, collect IdP logs and reconstruct.
3) Collect immutable audit chunks
   - Pull range from log store; verify chunk signatures and compute manifest hashes.
4) Package model-serving artifacts
   - Model version metadata, KV cache dumps (if needed), trace for inference path.
5) Redact and attest
   - Compliance Engineer runs redaction pipeline, produces attestation file listing redactions and rule ids.
6) Secure transfer & handoff
   - Encrypt bag with recipient key (Legal/External auditor) and log transfer event to audit store.
7) Close and archive
   - Mark manifest complete, move to long-term immutable archive per retention mapping.

Chain of custody checklist (must be recorded in manifest):
- Collected by (name, team, tool)
- Collection timestamp (UTC)
- Storage location & encryption key id
- Hashes (sha256) of artifacts
- Redaction attestation id
- Approvals for cross-border transfer (legal id)
- Recipient and transfer timestamp

Risk & exceptions process:
- Temporary exception types: retention extension, cross-border copy, full-raw export.
- Exception initiation: submit an Evidence Exception Request (EER) via policy portal with reason, owner, scope, and TTL.
- Approval chain: Evidence Owner -> Head of Security -> Legal (if cross-border or >30 days extension).
- Evidence of approval recorded in manifest under `exception_refs`.

Operational tooling and verification:
- Tools: `forensicctl` (collector), `ent-snap` (entitlement exporter), `logcat` (audit chunk verifier). Example commands:
  - `forensicctl collect --incident INC-2027-0423 --range 2027-02-11T13:50:00Z/2027-02-11T14:30:00Z --out s3://forensics/inc-2027/`
  - `ent-snap export --ts 2027-02-11T14:00:00Z --format ndjson > ent-snap.json`
  - `logcat verify --chunk s3://forensics/inc-2027/chunk-1.ndjson.gpg --pubkey /keys/forensic-pub.pem`

Testing and periodic exercises:
- Annual tabletop and quarterly collection drills. Drill artifacts must be marked `drill:true` in manifest and have 30-day retention.
- SDLC integration test: every major release must run a simulated evidence capture step as part of canary tests.

Appendices:
A. Evidence manifest JSON schema (flattened description)
- incident_id | string
- collected_at | iso8601
- collector | string
- artifacts | list of artifact descriptors (type, path, sha256, region, redacted)
- approvals | list (role, approver, timestamp, reason)

B. Quick redaction ruleset examples
- `PII_EMAIL` -> mask local-part, keep domain
- `CREDIT_CARD` -> store tokenized id only
- `CUSTOMER_CONTENT` -> hash and store reference unless explicit consent provided

C. Contacts
- SIR oncall: sir-oncall@redwood.ai
- Compliance Eng: compliance-eng@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
